newsitem.title: INDIA: Toyota chief hopes to meet Kirloskar.
newsitem.headline: Toyota chief hopes to meet Kirloskar.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp chairman Shoichiro Toyoda said on Friday he hopes to meet officials of the Kirloskar group, a possible joint venture partner, while leading a business mission to India.

"During the visit I would like to visit the Kirloskar group and extend my greetings to them," Toyoda, leading a Japan Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidanren) mission to India, told a news conference in New Delhi.

Toyoda, who is set on Monday to go to the southern city of Bangalore where he was expected to meet Kirloskar executives, reiterated that his car firm is studying the feasibility of jointly manufacturing cars in India.
Last March, Toyota broke off negotiations on a possible joint venture with Indian conglomerate Hinduja.
Last month Toyota director Hideaki Otaka said the Japanese company was in talks with Indian financial group Kirloskar to form a joint venture car plant in a location still to be decided.
Otaka said Toyota would take a stake of over 50 percent in the planned joint venture.

"I believe India has a very big future potential as a market," Toyoda said, adding that Toyota and Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd, a Toyota affiliate specialising in small cars, had joined hands in the feasibility study.
"We are now proceeding with feasibility studies anew," Toyoda said.

Earlier Otaka had said Toyota was expected to make multi-purpose or sports utility vehicles in India, and that Toyota and Kirloskar hoped to announce the final plan for a joint venture by the middle of this year.
Currently, Maruti Udyog Ltd, jointly controlled by Japan's Suzuki Motor Corp and the Indian government, holds a 70 percent share of the Indian car market.
Last year Toyota sold its remaining stake in Indian car maker DCM Daewoo Ltd to South Korea's Daewoo Corp . Toyota and Daewoo had been jointly assembling Toyota trucks since 1984.
"We were co-producing middle-size trucks," Toyoda said. "The market shrank and was not attractive any more. That is why we stopped this project."
